title: I have been making games for 20 years and Codex is blowing my mind.
author: startyourengines

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body: Codex is amazing, but I honestly feel Opus 5.5 is even better. And thst is without taking efficiency into account which honestly is terrible on Astra which basically leaves you no choice but to use Opus for any serious projects. I spend 100$ astra plan weekly limit in a day no matter what I do on my project

replies.author: Ball_Analytics
replies.body: I always used to think it was some bias thing, but when I worked they gave us cursor and I somehow hated using the chatGPT models second I discovered sonnet and opus. I got more done with less with the latter and found myself in a loop with the former. chatGPT has a tendency to please and results by any means policy which encourages it to cheat not realising its getting to the finish line without even running the race which means nothing's ultimately done.

replies.author: SeasawPhilosopher
replies.body: Dude opus 5.5 is so good at art and level design. I’m still using codex for code but I switched all my art needs to opus 5.5 two days ago. I reads my game bible, lore, level idea, and concept art and then talks like an art director imagining the setting, time of day, mood etc. It’s entirely different to how codex works for art and I’m getting super good results. It’ll think through the history of the level, the current weather, etc and hie that impacts wear, textures, etc.

comments.body: if u think codex is blowing your mind, try Opus 5.5 lol. Codex currently is a joke compared to Opus 5.5 for game creation

replies.author: VastReception1347
replies.body: I find them quite different in skills. In particular, codex has imagegen skill integrated that can generate textures and vector images. Opus on the other hand uses python. I was able to generate decent vector sprites with codex, whole opus did just a very schematic things. In other tasks Opus feels a bit faster and requires less iterations.

replies.author: Impressive_Award_679
replies.body:
Image-gen is imo the only upside of codex. Opus 5.5 is much better in 3D modelling and animations while also being much much much cheaper. Opus directly understands needs. The only relevant model comparable to opus from codex is astra which is (outside of you are rich) not really usable due to costs and in-efficiency. 

I mean there are good reasons why even codex users currently laugh about all other models. Sol 6, Luna 6, Sol 5.6 are even on xhigh a joke. They are making so making mistakes, so much unneccessary coding structures. Compared to Opus so much more worse in 3d modelling and animations. And even Astra has its flaws compared to Opus because it always tends to make stuff no one asked for, while Opus 5.5 does exactly, and only, what i asked for. 

Sure if your whole project relies on vector graphics and/or the image-gen structure, than codex might be the way to go, but if i take a look on the OPs game, he could make something even much cooler and better looking with Opus for a very "cheap" price.

replies.author: VastReception1347
replies.body:
Useful data point on 3D models and opus, I used codex thinking it would do a great job but it failed miserably, – will try Opus.

For context – I only use Astra in xhigh in codex, nothing else.

replies.author: Impressive_Award_679
replies.body:
Astra is fine. Its a good model. But sadly extremly expensive. 

Every ai model outside of trained 3d models will "suffer" to make really good 3d modells, but Opus 5.5 is definitly "ok" if you give it enough input, informations, references and so on. Detailed characters from scratch are still very hard. But objects, trees, flowers, bushes, walls, different building types are definitly FAR better than in any other codex model. 

If you combine this with for example mixamo, meshy/tripo, blender (mcp) it can be really good while being much cheaper than astra.
